chapter: Giving up and returning to music
title: The Silver Star, George Lewis and Slow Drag, then country picnics
summary: The band grows to six pieces around 1941 and plays the Silver Star, with George Lewis and Slow Drag sitting in, then picnics in the parishes.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That was around the thirties. Oh, yeah. The early thirties? No, no, forties. Oh, yeah. That's around 1941. Yeah. And I was over there at the time. Yeah. And we started getting plenty of work then. And we started to hire more men. Well, we played down here at the old Silver Star, down at St. Bernard and St. Claude. And we played down there for a couple of years on Friday, Saturdays and Sundays. Do you remember the rest of the band?
Who was in the rest of the band? No, I don't care.
There were so many different fellas, because every week we weren't able to get the same
But I know for one while there we had George Lewis and Slowdrag with us.
Well, they played a while with us until we got caught in the red and then we'd get the job up because we didn't like that idea, you know?

So we started playing down in the little country parishes. And every Sunday during the summer they had picnics down there where we'd go and they'd hire us to play the picnics. Yeah. It was mostly colored picnics and everything else. So one night, you know one Sunday afternoon, Eddie Morris needed a drummer. He was playing out here on Canal Boulevard at Linford's.
